title: Introduction to AI Systems & Infrastructure
subtitle: The foundation course: AI workload, compute, data & deployment basics
description: An introduction to the systems and infrastructure that power modern artificial intelligence. Students learn what AI workloads are, the compute, data, and software layers they depend on, and how AI systems are deployed across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments. The course threads a prototype-vs-production mindset throughout and previews the security, governance, and inference-serving topics that later certificate courses cover in depth. No prior AI experience required.
objectives: Define key AI concepts and terminology relevant to infrastructure planning.
Identify appropriate infrastructure components (compute, data, software) for specific AI workloads.
Evaluate cloud, on-premises, and hybrid deployment models against real requirements and constraints.
Apply responsible-AI and governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act at survey level) to infrastructure decisions.
Configure a basic, containerized AI development environment for building and testing.
slos: Define key AI concepts and terminology for infrastructure planning
Identify infrastructure components (compute/data/software) for a given AI workload
Evaluate cloud vs. on-prem vs. hybrid deployment models against requirements
Apply responsible-AI/governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act) to decisions
Configure a basic containerized AI development environment

weeks.title: Introduction to AI Infrastructure
weeks.summary: Frames the course's prototype-vs-production theme and orients students to AI infrastructure concepts.

weeks.title: AI Workloads & Infrastructure Requirements
weeks.summary: Distinguishes training vs. inference workloads and the infrastructure requirements each demands.

weeks.title: Computational Resources for AI
weeks.summary: Surveys computational resources for AI, including CPUs, GPUs, TPUs, and other accelerators.

weeks.title: AI Software Infrastructure

weeks.title: Data Infrastructure for AI
weeks.summary: Examines the data infrastructure that feeds AI systems, from storage to pipelines.

weeks.title: Cloud-Based AI Infrastructure
weeks.summary: Explores how AI infrastructure is provisioned and run on cloud platforms.

weeks.title: On-Premises AI Infrastructure
weeks.summary: Examines on-premises approaches to hosting and running AI infrastructure.

weeks.title: Hybrid Deployment Models & Midterm
weeks.summary: Covers hybrid cloud/on-prem deployment models; includes the course midterm exam.

weeks.title: Scaling AI Infrastructure
weeks.summary: Looks at scaling AI infrastructure, with an introduction to inference serving.

weeks.title: AI Infrastructure Security
weeks.summary: Surveys AI infrastructure security, including an overview of the OWASP LLM Top 10.

weeks.title: Monitoring, Logging & Observability
weeks.summary: Covers monitoring, logging, and observability practices for AI infrastructure.

weeks.title: Infrastructure for the AI Development Lifecycle

weeks.title: Ethical & Responsible AI Infrastructure

weeks.title: Cost Optimization for AI Infrastructure

weeks.title: AI Infrastructure Trends & Future Directions
weeks.summary: Discusses emerging trends and future directions in AI infrastructure.

weeks.title: Capstone Project & Course Review
weeks.summary: Students complete a final capstone project and review the course as a whole.
